blind_target.authors: Jiang, Y., Costello, P., & He, S.
blind_target.title: Processing of invisible stimuli: Advantage of upright faces and recognizable words in overcoming interocular suppression.
blind_target.evidence_quote:
The sole difference was that we used
the t-value and sample size reported by Jiang et al. (2007) to determine BFr0 (respectively,

blind_target.outcome_quote:
In light of the large BF10 , one could therefore
conclude that there is compelling evidence for a face inversion effect, but of a more modest

blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors support the tested effect; smaller effect magnitude does not change the verdict.

luna_triage.reason: The control experiment retests the upright-versus-inverted face suppression finding attributed to Jiang et al. (2007), and the Results report faster suppression for upright faces plus a direct replication Bayes factor comparison against Jiang et al. The only supplied shipped original is Hung et al. (2017), a distinct sound-shape mapping study; it does not represent Jiang et al. No prior adjudication file was available at the supplied path.
luna_triage.location: Methods, control experiment; Results, control experiment; References, Jiang et al. entry.
luna_triage.omission_quote: It is well-established in the CFS literature that upright faces break suppression faster than inverted faces (e.g., Jiang, Costello, & He, 2007; Stein, Sterzer, & Peelen, 2012), and replicating this effect would thus validate the presently employed paradigm.
